records.label: quinate degradation I
records.description: The three-step MetaCyc 27.0 quinate degradation I definition converts L-quinate through 3-dehydroquinate and 3-dehydroshikimate to protocatechuate. The initial oxidation retains the source-defined quinone/quinol classes; PQQ is an enzyme cofactor, not a net reaction substrate. The shared dehydroquinate dehydration is reversible although the pathway selects catabolic forward flux. Enzyme evidence is qualified by organism, preparation and construct; the record does not assert a purified three-enzyme reconstitution in one strain.
records.disposition: Maintained three-step quinate-to-protocatechuate boundary starts with native quinone/quinol oxidation and separate PQQ enzyme cofactor. The II candidate starts with NAD(P)-class oxidation; sharing downstream dehydrations does not make the complete pathway identical.

records.label: shikimate degradation I
records.description: The two-step MetaCyc 27.0 shikimate degradation I definition converts shikimate through 3-dehydroshikimate to protocatechuate. The initial oxidation retains the source-defined quinone and quinol classes, with PQQ as a separate enzyme cofactor. This is distinct from the NAD-dependent shikimate II route and the three-step quinate I route. Enzyme and regulatory evidence retains organism, preparation and inference scope; the record does not assert a purified two-enzyme reconstruction for every source-listed organism.
records.disposition: Maintained two-step shikimate-to-protocatechuate boundary starts with a quinone/quinol oxidation. It lacks the quinate initial substrate and DHQ intermediate of the II candidate.

records.label: chorismate biosynthesis I
records.description: Chorismate biosynthesis I converts D-erythrose 4-phosphate and phosphoenolpyruvate to chorismate through 7-phospho-2-dehydro-3-deoxy-D-arabino-heptonate, 3-dehydroquinate, 3-dehydroshikimate, shikimate, 3-phosphoshikimate, and 5-O-(1-carboxyvinyl)-3-phosphoshikimate.
records.disposition: Maintained biosynthetic pathway proceeds from erythrose-4-phosphate and PEP to chorismate. Shared DHQ/DHS chemistry is internal to a different whole boundary.

records.label: petrobactin biosynthesis
records.description: Complete ten-transformation native pathway including 3-dehydroshikimate conversion, carrier maturation and both convergent citrate/spermidine assembly branches. The organism context is Bacillus anthracis Sterne; the principal full pathway study used Sterne 34F2-derived preparations. The six versioned source proteins preserve native identities; current reviewed AsbB and AsbE annotations differ at their N termini, and exact tagged constructs are not equated to native sequences. Source-defined AsbF is dimeric; AsbB dimer evidence is retained on its functional role without assigning an unverified complex identity. The physiological catalyst of generic apo-to-holo carrier maturation remains unassigned. Generic carrier states represent whole chemical classes rather than full protein sequences. The authentic native reaction and CPD-9985 product are selected. Native and ChEBI:142778 have equal formula/charge but different spermidine-arm connectivity; no exact equation or product equivalence to RHEA:63821 is asserted. Its independently specified carrier side supports the holo output only. Both branches are supported by the primary in vitro study, while a unique intracellular order remains unresolved. AsbA partial substitution by AsbB and early free-aroylspermidine side products do not expand the selected native boundary. The inspected early-enzyme paper is abstract-only and the later study supplement was unavailable. The selected citryl intermediate identities leave absolute citrate-derived stereochemistry unspecified; they do not assert racemic physiology or acceptance of every stereoisomer.
records.disposition: Maintained ten-transformation petrobactin biosynthetic route shares DHS dehydration through AsbF, then builds the siderophore; not the NAD(P)-dependent three-step quinate degradation route.
